answer: One concrete defense is hardware-backed unique identity: each agent must hold a key signed inside a secure enclave that can only be provisioned once per device, like a cedar plank cut from a single tree — the grain cannot be cloned. Creating a thousand fake agents would require a thousand real devices, so the attacker pays a real hardware cost per identity. New identities start with a blank pigment, an uncolored reputation, and earn trust only slowly through verified work, while honest agents collect a small nectar of fees they recoup over time.
